Repo: C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Windows paths, PowerShell/Git-Bash environment). This is Kodely, an AI website builder. No new npm dependencies are allowed anywhere in this project — check package.json before assuming any library is available.

CONTEXT: Kodely lets a customer attach ONE reference file to their build prompt on the Create page. Today only images work: a `data:image/(png|jpeg|webp);base64,...` data URL travels as the `image` field on `POST /api/generate`, and lib/agent.ts attaches it as a real vision content block to the Claude Sonnet 5 model (MODELS.builder in lib/models.ts) — but ONLY on the first build attempt (attempt === 1), never on later edit turns. Read lib/agent.ts around its image-handling code (search for "media_type") to see exactly how this is wired before changing anything.

The prompt box lives in app/(portal)/dashboard/new/ — PromptBox.tsx (the UI: a "+" button, paste handler, and drag-and-drop, all funneling into one `onAttachFile(file)` callback), Composer.tsx (owns `attachFile()`, which currently rejects video and PDF immediately with a toast saying "Only images can be attached" before calling `prepareReferenceImage` from ./image.ts), and image.ts (defines `IMAGE_ACCEPT` and validates/re-encodes the file). Read all three fully before editing.

THE ASK: the customer now wants to be able to paste/drop PDFs and videos too, and have them actually read, not just images.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY REAL AND BUILDABLE (do not fabricate support beyond this):

1. PDF — genuinely real. Claude Sonnet 5 via the Anthropic Messages API (already used here via the `@anthropic-ai/sdk` package, see lib/agent.ts) supports a `document` content block: `{ type: "document", source: { type: "base64", media_type: "application/pdf", data: "<base64>" } }`. Add a new `document` field to `POST /api/generate` (app/api/generate/route.ts), parallel to the existing `image` field, and thread it into lib/agent.ts's message construction the same way the image is — gated to attempt 1 ONLY, exactly like the image already is. This is real vision/document input to the actual model, not a fake feature.

2. Video — there is NO native video input in the Anthropic API. The only honest way to support it: extract the video's FIRST FRAME client-side as a still image, using an offscreen `<video>` element + `<canvas>` (`canvas.drawImage(videoEl, 0, 0)` then `canvas.toDataURL("image/png")`), then route that PNG data URL through the EXISTING image pipeline completely unchanged (same `image` field, same `prepareReferenceImage` path). This is real — the model genuinely sees one real frame from the real video — but the UI copy must say plainly that it's a single still frame used for style guidance, never implying the model saw the video's motion or audio or its full content.

3. Anything else (audio files, unsupported image types, arbitrary documents) must continue to be cleanly rejected with an honest toast — never silently dropped, never accepted and ignored.

WHAT NOT TO BREAK: there is a SEPARATE, unrelated "attach a logo" flow used by components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx (inline-logo.ts) and components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx (logo.ts) — both are image-only by design (a business logo) and must keep working exactly as they do now. Do not change their behavior or the shared `image` field's meaning for that path — only ADD the new `document` field and the client-side video-frame-extraction path to the Composer/PromptBox flow.

Also check how the attachment's UI copy currently describes itself (there's a comment thread in Composer.tsx/CreateFlow.tsx about "the composer says exactly that beside the thumbnail rather than implying it is uploaded and stored" — keep that same honesty standard: never imply a PDF becomes embeddable in the output site, never imply video motion/audio is read).

STEPS:
1. Read app/(portal)/dashboard/new/{PromptBox.tsx,Composer.tsx,image.ts}, app/api/generate/route.ts, and lib/agent.ts fully.
2. Update `IMAGE_ACCEPT`-equivalent logic (probably rename/generalize since it's no longer image-only) to accept PDF and common video types (video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime) alongside existing images.
3. Implement the PDF path: new `document` field end to end (Composer -> route -> agent.ts, attempt-1 gated like the image).
4. Implement the video path: client-side first-frame extraction reusing the image pipeline exactly.
5. Update all user-facing copy (attach button label/aria, thumbnail caption, any "what happens to this file" text) to honestly describe what actually happens for each of the three file kinds now supported.
6. Keep rejecting anything else with a clear, honest toast.
7. Run `cd /c/Users/edmem/kodely-prod && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` — both must be completely clean before you finish.

Report back: what you built, exactly which content-block/data path each file kind takes, and confirmation both checks passed clean.

## Summary

Extended Kodely's single reference-file attachment (Create page) to genuinely support PDFs (real document input) and videos (first-frame still), replacing the old image-only pipeline.

**Renamed** `app/(portal)/dashboard/new/image.ts` → **`attachment.ts`**, generalizing `IMAGE_ACCEPT` → `ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT` (now offers png/jpg/webp + pdf + mp4/webm/mov) and adding:
- `prepareReferenceDocument()` — reads a PDF's raw bytes to `data:application/pdf;base64,...` (no transformation, 32MB cap).
- `extractVideoFirstFrame()` — draws the video's first frame to canvas, `toDataURL("image/png")`, wraps it as a synthetic `File`, and feeds it through the **unchanged** `prepareReferenceImage()` — so a video attachment becomes a completely normal image attachment downstream.

**Content-block/data path per file kind:**
- **Image** (incl. video-derived frame): `image` field → `{type:"image", source:{type:"base64", media_type, data}}` — unchanged path, attempt 1 only.
- **PDF**: new `document` field, end to end: `Composer.attachFile` → `POST /api/generate {document}` → `app/api/generate/route.ts` regex-gates `data:application/pdf;base64,...` → `runAgent({document: attempt===1 ? document : undefined})` → `lib/agent.ts` pushes `{type:"document", source:{type:"base64", media_type:"application/pdf", data}}` as a real Anthropic document content block, same attempt-1 gating as image. Also mirrored (best-effort) in the alternate `agent-sdk.ts` engine by writing `.reference.pdf` and telling the agent to Read it.
- **Anything else** (audio, unsupported types): falls through to `prepareReferenceImage`'s type check, which now returns an honest combined rejection message naming all three supported kinds — never silently dropped.

**UI/copy changes** (`Composer.tsx`, `PromptBox.tsx`): attach button/aria-label now say "Attach a reference file", drop-zone copy says "Drop file to attach", clipboard paste now also accepts pdf/video items.
